subject: Demo recap & POC plan — HealthTech Solutions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Johnson <alicia.johnson@healthtech-solutions.com>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@healthtech-solutions.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap & proposed POC plan — HealthTech Solutions

Hi Alicia / Marcus,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really appreciate the open discussion about your indexing and search workflows for patient-facing clinical content. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we can get aligned on success criteria and next steps.

Key takeaways from the demo:
- You want sub-200ms average token latency on search/answer flows for web UI.
- Host on a private VPC instance (data residency in us-west) and keep logs for 90 days.
- Target throughput: ~10 concurrent user sessions with bursts up to 30 QPS.
- Primary model family: open-llm tuned for summarization + retrieval.

Proposed 3-week POC (outline attached: poe-eval-plan.xlsx):
1) Week 0 (Kickoff): access + sandbox dataset ingest (we provide S3/ingest instructions).
2) Week 1 (Integration): connect your retrieval layer to Redwood’s API + baseline latency/cost run.
3) Week 2 (Evaluation): run evaluation prompts and synthetic load; capture latency, p99, and quality metrics vs your scoring set.
4) Week 3 (Wrap & Decision): present results, hit acceptance criteria, and agree next steps.

Success criteria (suggested, open to your edits):
- Latency: median < 150ms, p95 < 350ms for typical query sizes.
- Quality: 80%+ on your relevance/accuracy rubric across the evaluation prompt set.
- Cost: projected token cost meets your target TCO for expected QPS.
- Security: sandbox in your VPC, logs retained 90d, SOC2 controls verified.

Ownership / contacts:
- Redwood: Marissa (solution lead), Rishi (sales lead) — see CCs.
- HealthTech: Alicia (product lead), Marcus (CTO).

Immediate next steps:
- Confirm POC scope + success criteria by end of week.
- I’ll provision a sandbox project and share access + the evaluation prompt set.
- Please confirm who on your side will own data ingestion and test harness.

Attachments: poe-eval-plan.xlsx (POC timeline & eval plan)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if you want to walk through the plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Alicia Johnson <alicia.johnson@healthtech-solutions.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@healthtech-solutions.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap & POC plan — HealthTech Solutions

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap and the attached plan. A few clarifying questions before we lock the plan in:

1) Data residency: we need all inference to run in our VPC in us-west and no logging of PHI. Is Redwood able to support a no-logs mode for the POC?
2) Throughput: the 10 concurrent sessions number is correct, but our worst-case burst could be up to 50 QPS for short periods. Can you confirm vertical scaling options?
3) Evaluation harness: who will own running the relevance scoring harness — our team or Redwood? We prefer to run locally but can use the Redwood sandbox if it’s easier.

Also — Marcus asked if we can shorten the POC to two weeks (kickoff + one week integration + one week evaluation) if we scope down the ingestion to a 10k-document sample. Will that be feasible?

I’ve attached our security intake matrix (security-questionnaire.pdf) — let me know if you need anything else.

Thanks,
Alicia
Product Lead — Search & Discovery
HealthTech Solutions

Thanks Alicia — great questions. Short answers below and a couple of proposed adjustments to the plan to keep timeline tight.

1) Data residency / no-logs: Yes — we can provision a private VPC deployment for the POC and enable a no-logs mode for inference (we’ll sign an addendum). We’ll also provide a minimal audit log for operational debugging that can be redacted.
2) Throughput & scaling: Redwood Dedicated autoscaling can handle short bursts; for a 50 QPS short burst we recommend enabling small burst capacity (we can provision 2x baseline GPUs for test windows). I’ve noted this as an optional line item in the attached SLA doc (redwood-poc-sla.pdf).
3) Evaluation harness ownership: we recommend a split approach — HealthTech runs your relevance scoring locally against the evaluation set while Redwood runs the same prompts in the sandbox and returns the raw outputs so you can score them. This minimizes data transfer of sensitive content.

On the timeline: we can compress to 2 weeks if we limit ingestion to a 10k-document sample and agree to a skinny acceptance criteria set (latency + relevance on core flows). I’ve updated the attached evaluation plan to show a 2-week option.

Next steps I’ll action this week:
- Provision a sandbox project and share access (Marissa) — target: Wed EOD.
- Schedule 30-min kickoff with your engineering lead to review ingest options (please share contact).
- Rishi / Neha — can you confirm resource availability for a 2-week compressed POC and any promotional credit we can extend?

Attachments: redwood-poc-sla.pdf

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
